extracted.intended_audience: Grantee institution staff using eRA Commons (Principal Investigators, Signing Officials, FSRs, Grants Management Specialists)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and content requirements for viewing application status and for completing closeout-related submissions in eRA Commons (Final Invention Statement, Final Progress Report, FFR, PRAM/FRAM, relinquishing statements, etc.). Focused on PI, SO, and FSR roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Invention Statement (FIS) — deadline and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit a Final Invention Statement within 90 days following the termination of a grant award. The statement should include all inventions that were conceived or first reduced to practice during the course of work under the grant or award, from the original effective date of support through the date of completion or termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All actions are performed from the Submit Final Invention Statement screen (accessed via Closeout Status). The FIS must list inventions conceived or first reduced to practice during the project period. Refer to the Procedure for Submission of Final Invention Statement and Certification for additional policy details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Invention Statement (FIS) — roles, certification, and status
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a Signing Official (SO) can submit the FIS to the Agency; a PI can create the FIS but the SO must verify and submit it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a PI saves an invention the status is 'Awaiting SO Verification'; when an SO saves it may be 'Saved'; after SO submission status becomes 'Received' and 'Verified by <name>' with a View action. Upon submission you cannot update the FIS. A certification popup text is presented on save/submit ('I hereby certify that...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Invention Statement (FIS) — adding/updating/removing inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: SOs and PIs may add inventions to the FIS via the Add Invention screen by providing required fields (Title of Invention; Name of Inventor; Date Reported to DHHS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat 'Add Invention' steps for each invention. To remove an invention use the Remove link in the Saved Invention section. To change a saved FIS, select Change and re-select Yes/No or add/remove inventions; then Save. If you need to hold off, select Cancel rather than Submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Invention Statement (FIS) — claiming no inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: You may create a Final Invention Statement certifying that no inventions exist by selecting 'No' on the Submit Final Invention Statement screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certification statement popup will read: 'I hereby certify that, to the best of my knowledge and belief, no inventions were conceived or first actually reduced to practice during the course of work under the referenced DHHS grant or award for the specified period.' Save to update status to 'Saved' (then SO verifies/submits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Progress Report (FPR) — requirement and minimum content
rubrics_metrics.description: A Final Progress Report is required for any grant that has ended and any grant that is not to be extended through award of a new competitive segment. This report should be prepared in accordance with instructions provided by the awarding component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a minimum the Final Progress Report should include: (1) A statement of progress made towards the achievement of originally stated aims; (2) A list of results (positive and/or negative) considered significant; (3) A list of publications resulting from the project, including plans, if any, for further publication. A copy of reprints or publications not previously submitted should accompany the FPR. If publications have been submitted to PubMed Central (PMC), a reference to the PMC submission identification number may be included instead of a hard copy. Reports on inclusion of gender and minority study subjects (using the gender and minority inclusion table as provided in the PHS2590), indication of whether children were involved or how the study was relevant for conditions affecting children, and a description of data/research materials/protocols/software available to be shared and how to access them should also be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Progress Report (FPR) — acceptable substitutions and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If a competitive renewal (Type 2) has been submitted, whether funded or not, the progress report contained in that application may serve in lieu of a separate Final Progress Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the discretion of the awarding unit, a reprint or pre-print may be used as the FPR. Grantees should contact their assigned Grants Management Specialist for information on these alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Progress Report (FPR) — format and submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Closeout - Upload Final Progress Report screen allows you to upload your Final Progress Report. The report must be in Adobe PDF format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select Choose File to pick the PDF and Submit. A certification popup is displayed upon submission. When saved/submitted the report status updates to 'Received' and the Action column contains the View FPR link. If Program Officer requests additional info, a FRAM Update link will appear for submitting additional material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Progress Report Additional Materials (FRAM)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FRAM feature provides a means for grantees to enter, review, route, and submit information in response to specific request(s) by the Program Official for additional information related to the Final Progress Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Program Officer determines additional information is needed upon review of the FPR, they will request FRAM and a FRAM Update link appears in the Action column. Use the FRAM workflow to supply requested materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout policy — timely submission and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Closeout includes timely submission of all required reports and adjustments for amounts due the grantee or NIH. Closeout does not automatically cancel requirements for property accountability, record retention, or financial accountability. Following Closeout, the grantee remains obligated to return funds due, and the Federal Government may recover amounts based on audit results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will close out grants as soon as possible after expiration or termination. Closeout interfaces with Agency staff Closeout system to track and monitor completion of requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout timeline and unilateral closeout policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutes/Centers (ICs) are directed to initiate a unilateral closeout (closeout without the cooperation of the grantee) 180 days after the project end date if it has not received acceptable final reports required by the award terms. After making reasonable efforts, ICs must close all awards no later than 270 days after the project end date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While 'In Unilateral Closeout' some action links may still be available unless disabled by Grants Management Staff; when 'Unilaterally Closed' links will not be available. Screen text will indicate unilateral closeout status and date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Financial Report (FFR) — purpose and FSR role
rubrics_metrics.description: A Federal Financial Report (FFR) is a statement of expenditures associated with a grant. Recipients of federal funds are required to complete an FFR to report the status of funds to the sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users with the FSR role can search for grants and FFRs for their institution and may Create, View, Submit, and Revise FFRs. The FSR role can access the FFR module from the Closeout Status screen. Refer to Commons Online Help or the Federal Financial Report (FFR) Expenditure Data User Guide PDF for detailed instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress Report Additional Materials (PRAM) and IC-Requested PRAM
rubrics_metrics.description: The Progress Report Additional Materials (PRAM) screen is used for submitting Public Access PRAM and IC Requested PRAM in response to PRAM requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institute/Center PRAM Requests screen provides read-only access to IC PRAM requests and data: Identifying Information (link to read-only copy of I/C PRAM Request details), Requested Date, Number of Reminders Sent, Last Reminder Sent Date. The consolidated Progress Report Additional Materials file opens as a PDF formatted with an information header for each PRAM submission followed by attached documents; multiple submissions are separated and displayed most recent first; bookmarks are provided for navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion enrollment data submission path (IMS vs. RPPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit inclusion enrollment data with a progress report, IMS must be accessed via the RPPR Section G. Special Reporting Requirements rather than through the Inclusion link in the Status module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Inclusion link in the Status module provides access to IMS for viewing/managing inclusion enrollment data for off-cycle reporting before the progress report is due, but must NOT be used to submit inclusion data with an RPPR. Refer to the NIH and Other PHS Agency RPPR Instruction Guide for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additions for Review — SRO-supplied materials and categories
rubrics_metrics.description: After application submission, an SRO may upload additional material that clarifies or supplements the original submission; when uploaded it is available via the Status Information screen under Additions for Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Additions for Review screen displays top-level grant info (Grant Number, PI Name(s), Project Title, Appl. Status, Institution, Appl ID) and specific info for each uploaded item: Group (category: Updated Pages; Supplemental Material; Collaboration Letters; Modified Budget Pages; Accepted Publication; Biographical Sketches; Other), Document (filename link to open), and Date (date uploaded). Uploaded documents can be viewed, updated, and saved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Supplements — purpose and displayed fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Supplements are requests for (or the award of) additional funds during a current project period to provide for an increase in costs due to unforeseen circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrative Supplements screen (read-only) displays general grant info and a table (option to show Current Support Year or All Support Years) with columns: Identifying information (grant number link opens Administrative Supplement Request PDF), Accession Number, Supplement Status, Submitted Date, Comments for Grantee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishing Statement — change of institution requirement and fields
rubrics_metrics.description: A relinquishing statement is required as part of the Change of Institution process allowing an extramural grantee institution to transfer an active grant to another institution; the process is initiated by the Signing Official of the institution that holds the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relinquishing Statements screen provides read-only access to all relinquishing statements associated with the grant and displays Document Name (link to read-only form), Status, Submitted Date, and Comments for the Grantee. The Relinquishing Statement feature allows editing and re-routing of the electronic relinquishing statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing Summary Statements and Notices of Award (NOA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary Statements (PDFs combining reviewers' written comments and the SRO summary) and Notices of Grant Award (NOA) are accessible via the Status Information screen once released or issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To view Summary Statement: log into Commons > Status > List of Applications/Grants > select application ID > Other Relevant Documents > Summary Statement link (opens in separate window). NOAs are sent to the email specified in the Institutional Profile (SO can update) and are available in Status Information as a date next to 'Notice(s) of Grant Award (PDF)'; selecting the NOA link opens it in a separate window.
